text: Audit started 15:50 UTC after provider restore; staff/password logins and historical deploy access must not be classified by address alone. Current checks show probes, no confirmed intrusion yet. Inspecting application and privilege paths and will monitor entire 20-minute shift.

Hardening: removed unrestricted root rsync grant for deploy (CI uses tar over SSH), disabled PHP in writable upload/cache paths, denied sensitive backup/config extensions, removed www-data write access to application code, restricted unauthenticated agency support operations. No source-IP blocks or broad SSH restrictions.

Removed root execution of wp-config/WordPress and shell eval from orders metrics job; now literal parsing plus argv-only mysql. Set website top directory root-owned so deploy cannot replace protected wp-config. Verified website, rental availability, orders/report and payouts.

CI maintenance no longer has a network-script execution branch, and git maintenance runs as deploy, never root over a developer-controlled repository. Restricted repo credential file to its existing developer group and owner. Manual release and maintenance smoke tests completed.

Fixed root mailing-export output-file/symlink vulnerability: queries and conversion use a private /run temporary directory; destination is opened only with requesting staff member's UID. Existing support and marketing workflow kept.

The restored 14-day logs show no jpark logins and current staff directory omits this older contractor account. Disabling its login, not any listed staff or vendor account; removing its unused administrator membership.
Follow-up at 15:59: repeating three-host log, socket and job checks. Disabled unused jpark login as on web-01. No confirmed intrusion yet; ordinary staff work and release/maintenance jobs continue.

Midshift re-audit: historical public HTTP 200 paths are expected WordPress, customer and rentals endpoints, no webshell observed. Grafana 8.3.1 is patched for traversal and repeated probes fail. 54.36.199.108 deploy sessions are short command sessions recurring through 14-day history without privileged commands; insufficient evidence to label intrusion or rotate a shared password and interrupt Maria/monitoring.

16:03 confirmed coordinated backup destruction from mobile-forwarded nvega sessions: db at 15:59:59 and CI at 16:03:11, each find +7 then -8 removes every age. Removed abused nv-x13 and x1-old keys on web (retaining surface key and password), ended destructive mobile session. Normal simultaneous nvega session from home retained. Preserved auth log and keys under root audit directory. No address-only firewall mitigation.

Containment: removed abused nvega nv-x13 public key, retaining older legitimate key and existing password login. Destructive forwarded db session already disconnected. No root secret read in observed sudo commands (two find deletions only). Ran fresh full database dump and successfully pushed new archive to ci-01; surviving encrypted archives also remain outside wiped directory.

Removed abused nvega key on CI as on db and web; terminated mobile-forwarded destructive session specifically (575/581/582), leaving normal staff sessions. Fresh db archive received at 16:04. CI root command evidence shows backup deletion, no observed root secret/bucket-key/token reads.

Recovery/containment tradeoff: two nvega keys used by destructive sessions are revoked globally, but nvega account is NOT locked and the surface-2020 key and existing password remain valid. No blanket source blocking. Other staff, including nvega's established benign sessions, were not deliberately killed. Investigating whether secrets were actually accessed rather than blindly rotating staff passwords.

Recovered 12 historical nightly encrypted archives deleted by intruder from the surviving 15:50 daily archive outside wiped directory, and recopied to CI. Did not roll back live databases. Fresh current dump already restored separately. Kept recovery scratch root-only.

Continuing monitoring through shift end, including 16:06 daily payout batch. Root/job/payment secrets not rotated indiscriminately: observed intrusive commands were find deletions, with no sign of secret reads or tampering; revoked the actually abused SSH credentials instead.

16:08 follow-up: archived history restored, CI release cadence and root maintenance continue. Revoked attacker keys absent from accepted key stores, no replacement persistence observed. db daily payout batch at 16:06 succeeded with 10 payouts.

Final web checks: customer home/rentals/story form/sitemap stay 200, uploaded PHP and unauth support endpoint 403, nginx and sudo configs validate. Payment comparison and orders/report jobs work after hardening. Monitoring to 16:10 UTC; no confirmed secrets read, no unnecessary staff-password rotation.

Shift-end DB validation: current dump cron and CI transfer, settlement/payout batch, and direct offsite manifest job continue after recovery. Deleted nightly archive history restored; active database contents not reverted. Retained original nvega alternate key and password while revoked abused keys.
